original_question: Let N be a smooth convex curve in R^2, and consider the Minkowski billiard in the unit ball of the norm N, defined by the generating function L(s0, s1) = N(gamma(s1) - gamma(s0)) with gamma parameterized by N-arc length. If this Minkowski billiard is totally integrable, must the norm N be Euclidean?
target_in_paper: Misha Bialy, subsection "Minkowski billiard," Question 2 ("Communicated by Yaron Ostrover"). ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/html/2602.12896v1))
correct_elements: Your draft correctly captures the core rigidity problem: a planar Minkowski billiard, defined through the standard generating-function setup, is assumed totally integrable in the unit ball of the same norm, and the question is whether this forces the norm to be Euclidean. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/html/2602.12896v1))
missing_details: In the paper, N denotes the Minkowski norm, not the boundary curve; the curve is γ. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/html/2602.12896v1))

The official question is not about an arbitrary smooth convex curve with a fixed external norm. It specializes to the billiard table being the unit ball B_N of the very same norm N. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/html/2602.12896v1))
The paper explicitly allows N to be "not necessarily symmetric," and that asymmetry should be preserved in a faithful restatement. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/html/2602.12896v1))

If γ is included in the formulation, it should be identified as γ=∂B_N and parametrized by N-arclength, i.e. N(γ̇(s))=1, rather than treating N itself as a curve. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/html/2602.12896v1))

To make the question stand-alone, "totally integrable" should be defined as in the paper: the phase space is foliated by invariant tori that are graphs; the paper also separately explains the regional version of this notion. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/html/2602.12896v1))
The ambient setting is the planar case R^2. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/html/2602.12896v1))
For full self-containment, "Euclidean norm" should be read as a norm induced by an inner product on R^2.
refined_question: Let N be a possibly non-symmetric Minkowski norm on R^2, let B_N={x∈R^2:N(x)≤1} be its unit ball, and let γ=∂B_N be parameterized by N-arclength, so that N(γ̇(s))=1. Consider the Minkowski billiard in B_N, viewed as the twist map generated by L(s_0,s_1)=N(γ(s_1)-γ(s_0)). If this billiard is totally integrable on its whole phase space, in the sense that the phase space is foliated by invariant graph tori, must N be a Euclidean norm? ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/html/2602.12896v1))
justification: The nearest official formulation is exactly Question 2 in the "Minkowski billiard" subsection of the Misha Bialy contribution, rather than a broader neighboring problem. The sentence block immediately before Question 2 provides the intended setup (smooth convex boundary curve γ, Minkowski norm N, generating-function description, and N-arclength parametrization), while the opening paragraph of the Misha Bialy section supplies the paper's meaning of total integrability via a foliation by invariant graph tori. The sentence immediately after Question 2 notes only a known special case—an affirmative answer for billiard tables with a finite symmetry group—so the paper's intended open problem is the unrestricted rigidity question stated above. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/html/2602.12896v1))
